title: Time with Chris Kelly and his band members
summary: Howard worked side jobs with Chris, later took Sam Morgan's place; he names Chris's drummer and sidemen.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Yeah. Let me turn it off before the knife comes home. So we have a pretty good idea what Chris played like from that. Yeah, that's it. Well how long were you with that first band before you went with Chris?
With Son Leger and? With Son Leger? Well quite a while. I just remember the exact time I played with them.
Would you say closer to a year, six months, two years?
Maybe about six months or something like that, or maybe a little more.
And how long were you with Chris?
Well I never was a regular man with him, but he played side jobs, you know, different kids.
I see.

And I played, after I started playing the trumpet, I played a lot of times with him. And when Sam died I'd taken his place quite a while with Izil Muggenbaum. I still moved up from second to first and I played the second.
I see. With the band. Who was Chris's regular drummer then?
Well, Roy Evans.
Roy Evans, yeah. Yeah, Roy. Roy was a wonderful drummer. Wonderful. Do you remember who would be members of Chris's band then?

Well it's about the same thing like the bands go now, they would change about it. But he had George for quite a while, and Georgia Boy, Zeb, Guy used to play the banjo mostly with him, Peter Papin, he played with him, Yank Johnson, Yank Johnson and Buddy Johnson, Yank's brother, they used to play, Earl Unford, he was his trombone player most of the time. And Chester Lazardi, bass man.
Did he use a piano ever?
I never remember Chris having a piano.
Saxophone ever? Yeah, he had saxophone.
I think Edward Gome used to play with him too. He used to play sax with him.
Which saxophone was that?
Alto sax.
He used alto more.

Alto sax and he had a fellow by the name of Pajot played, he's a barber, his name was Pajot, he used to play ten of sax with him. Well that would be mostly when they played at the Bulls Club, they'd have two or three bands every Tuesday night, where they'd have eight men's, eight or nine men's in each band.
